findings.residual_open: why the two bases' 24-cell admission tables agree, hence why the graph is common, is not decided here
findings.thesis: The two bases' holonomy class-count profiles agree because their two connections are ONE point of the 4,096-element connection space on the common gauge-fixed graph, and that point is forced -- cycle by cycle -- by four species clauses both bases satisfy: a preparation leg common to the two frames, commuting local legs, a wing exchange that intertwines the local legs at a symmetric setting, and a wing exchange that does NOT intertwine the preparation leg. The agreement is not a 2.5% coincidence; the two bases are not two independent draws.

evidence.note: the declaration itself is a disclosure; its teeth are the freeze gate before it and the consistency gate after it

chain.clause: E0  the two rules draw different maps at t=0 (admission table)
E1  the preparation leg is common to the two frames
E2  the two local legs commute
E3  the wing exchange intertwines both local legs
E4  the wing exchange does not intertwine the preparation leg

evidence.note: the third instance: fresh quaternion, different preparation, different completion
the exchange-equivariant control: the bare Householder

evidence.declared_group: one Klein-group value per node, the constant subgroup fixed by the declared section h(F1@t0)=1
evidence.note: with the correct convention the invariance is analytically forced: a closed walk enters and leaves every node the same number of times, so a node-valued gauge telescopes away; the measurement is that the instrument implements that convention

evidence.declared_group: one Klein-group value per node, the constant subgroup fixed by the declared section h(F1@t0)=1

evidence.note: analytically forced: every element of the group is an involution

C1 source-split.statement: the full-leg sub-connection is flat, the realized-rule sub-connection carries a group of order two, every two-rule coordinate has a non-flat bigon, and the whole connection generates the group

C10 group of order four.statement: the connection's labels generate a group of order four -- the explanation the generality unit offered

C2a aut-equivariance (rule-preserving).statement: invariant under the induced action of the rule-preserving automorphism group of the graph

C2b aut-equivariance (full).statement: invariant under the induced action of the full multigraph automorphism group

C2c aut-equivariance up to naming.statement: for every graph automorphism there is an automorphism of the Klein group carrying the pullback back to the connection

C3 admission-pattern.statement: every coordinate at which the two rules draw DIFFERENT permutations carries a non-flat bigon -- the only constraint the 24-cell table places on a connection

C4 species-split (named).statement: the six declared cycles take the values the species clauses force, with the group elements named: (1, 1, D, 1, 1, W)

C5 species-split (naming-closed).statement: there are distinct non-identity d, w with the six declared cycles at (1, 1, d, 1, 1, w)

C6 common preparation leg.statement: the full-leg square around the preparation leg is flat (the two frames share that leg)

C7 commuting local legs.statement: the canonical loop is flat (the two local legs commute)

C8 intertwined local legs.statement: the two realized-rule squares around the local legs are flat (the wing exchange intertwines them)

C9 unintertwined preparation leg.statement: the realized-rule square around the preparation leg is neither flat nor the wing exchange
